FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Pesticides 
Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division Council. 


Tricyclazole wettable granules (WG) is used as fungicide in agriculture. 


In the formulation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of Insecticides Act, 1968 and 
the Rules framed thereunder. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under the /nsecticides 
Act and Rules, wherever applicable. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)’. The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 17202 : 2019 


Indian Standard 


TRICYCLAZOLE WETTABLE GRANULES (WG) — 
SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirement and the 
methods of sampling and test for Tricyclazole wettable 
granules (WG). 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards listed below contain provisions which 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions 
of this standard .At the time of publications, the 
editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject 
to revision, and parties to agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of the standards 
listed below. 


IS No Title

their formulations (first revision)

: 1990 Part 1 General requirements (second 
revision)

formulations 
15982: 2013  Tricyclazole, Technical — 
Specification 


3 REQUIREMENTS 


3.1 Constituents 


3.1.1 The material shall consist of Tricyclazole 
Technical along with suitable carrier(s), stabilizers(s), 
and other formulant (s) 


technical 
material 


3.1.2 Tricyclazole 
formulation of this 
IS 15982. 


employed in the 
shall conform to 


3.2 Description 


The material shall be in the form of tan to brick red 
colored free flowing odorless granules and shall wet 
readily on mixing with water providing a suspension 
for suitable use as spray. 


3.3 The material shall also comply with the requirements 


: 1988 pesticides: Part 1 Solid pesticides given in Table 1. 
(second revision)

3.3.1 When determined by the method prescribed in 
Annex A , the observed tricyclazole content, percent 
(m/m) of any of the samples shall not differ from

4 PACKING 


The material shall be packed in trilaminated pouch 
with material of construction of 12 microns PET/9 
microns Al foil/75-85 microns poly, which shall be 
packed in secondary pack of duplex board/3 ply E 
fluted carton conforming to IS 2771 (Part 1). This 
carton shall be further packed in 5-ply corrugated 
fibre board box as a transport pack conforming to 
IS 2171 (Part 1). The capacity of the pouches shall be 
60 gm, 120 gm, 240 gm and 480 gm. These shall be 
properly heat sealed to make these leak proof and pilfer 
proof. The packaging shall also conform to the general 
requirements as given in IS 8190 (Part 1). 


5 MARKING 


5.1 The containers shall be securely closed and 
the following information shall be marked legibly 
and indelibly on each container in addition to any 
other information as is necessary under the 
Insecticides Act, 1968 and rules framed there under: 


a) Name of the material; 

b) Name ofthe manufacturer; 

c) Date of manufacture; 

d) Batch number; 

e) Net mass of the contents; 

f) Tricyclazole content, percent (m/m); and 


g) A cautionary notice worded as in the Insecticides 
Act, 1968 and Rules. 


5.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the Bureau 
of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules and 
Regulations framed thereunder, and the products may 
be marked with the Standard Mark . 


6 SAMPLING 


When freshly manufactured material is offered for 
inspection, representative samples shall be drawn 
according to IS 10627 and tested within 90 days of its 
manufacture. However, the criteria for conformity of the 
material when tested shall be the limits of tolerances, as 
applicable over the declared nominal value and given 
under 3.3.1 of this standard. 


7 TESTS 


7.1 Tests shall be carried out by the appropriate methods 
referred in 3.3 and col 4 and 5 of Table 1. 


7.2 Quality of Reagents 


Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and distilled 
water (IS 1070) shall be employed in tests. 


NOTE — ‘Pure chemicals’ shall mean chemicals that do not 
contain impurities, which affect the results of analysis. 


IS 17202 : 2019 


ANNEX A 
[ Clause 3.3.1 and Table 1, SI No. (i) ] 


DETERMINATION OF TRICYCLAZOLE CONTENT 


A-0 GENERAL 


Two methods namely, High Performance 
Liquid Chromatography (HPLC), or Gas Liquid 
Chromatography may be used for determination of 
Tricyclazole Content. However, either the HPLC or 
GLC shall be the referee methods. 


A-1 GAS LIQUID CHROMATOGRAPHY 
(GLC) METHOD 
A-1.1 Principle 


Tricyclazole content is determined by Gas Liquid 
Chromatography (GLC) with Flame lonisation 
Detector (FID) using internal standard technique. 


A-1.2 Apparatus 


A-1.2.1 Gas Liquid Chromatograph (GLC), equipped 
with FID and chromatography software/printer cum 
integrator. 


A-1.2.2 Analytical Balance - least count - 0.1 mg 
A-1.2.3 Microlitre Syringe, 10 uL capacity. 
A-1.2.4 Ultrasonic Bath 

A-1.2.5 Standard Glassware 


A-1.3 Chromatographic Conditions 


The following are the suggested analytical conditions 
for the determination of tricyclazole content in 
WG samples . These conditions may be varied , if 
nececessary provided standardization is done: 


Instrument Gas chromatograph (GLC) 
equipped with FID and 
chromatography software/printer 
cum integrator. 

Stationery Phase: 5 percent SE-30 ( or equivalent) 
on chromosorb WHP, (100/120) 
mesh. 6’ x 2.0 mm ID Glass 

Temperature 

Column oven 250° C 

Injector 260° C 

Detector 270° C 

Gas flow rates 

Nitrogen (carrier): 30 ml/min. 

Hydrogen 30 ml / min. 

Air 300 ml / min. 


A-1.4 Reagents 
A-1.4.1 Acetone — AR grade 


A-1.4.2 Internal Standard 
grade 


Di Octyl phthalate — AR 


A-1.4.3 Tricyclazole — Reference standard of known 
purity. 


A-1.5 Procedure 


A-1.5.1 Preparation of Internal Standard 


Weigh accurately about 2.5 g of di-octyl phthalate into a 
100 ml volumetric flask. Dissolve in acetone and make 
up the volume up to the mark with acetone. Shake well 
to homogenize. 


A-1.5.2 Preparation of Standard Solution 


Weigh accurately about 0.25-0.30 g of tricyclazole 
reference standard of known purity into a 25 ml 
volumetric flask. Add 5 ml of the internal standard 
solution (see A-1.4.1) and make up to the mark with 
Acetone. Shake well to homogenize. 


A-1.5.3 Preparation of Formulation Sample Solution 


Weigh sample equivalent to 0.25-0.30 g of tricyclazole 
WG formulation sample into a 25 ml volumetric flask. 
Add 5 ml of internal standard solution (see A-1.4.1) 
and make up the volume up to the mark with Acetone. 
Shake well to homogenize. 


A-1.6 Estimation 


A-1.6.1 Inject 1 ul of tricyclazole standard solution 
into the gas chromatograph , using a microliter syringe 
(10 ul) ‚until area of tricyclazole and internal standard 
in replicate injections matches within + 2 percent. 
Inject WG sample solutions and note down the peak 
areas of both. Inject the standard and sample solution 
according to A-1.6.2 and then compute the percentage 
purity of tricyclazole in WG sample using the formula 
given in A-1.8. 


A-1.6.2 Sequence of injection to be followed — Cl, 
C2, SIA, SIB, C2, C1, S2A, S2B, C2. 
A-1.7 Retention Time (Guide Values) 

Tricyclazole ~ 3.5 min. 

Di-octyl phthalate ~ 8.0 min. 


Total run time ~ 12 min. 


IS 17202 : 2019 


A-1.8 Calculation 


Tricyclazole content, 
percent m/m = 


M, x A,x A, x P 


M,x A, XA, 
where, 
,= Mass in g, of standard tricyclazole in standard 
solution; 
M,= Mass in ,g of sample taken for test; 
A, = Area of tricyclazole peak in the chromatogram 
of standard solution; 
A,= Area of tricyclazole peak in the chromatogram 
of sample solution; 
A,= Area of internal standard peak in the 
chromatogram of standard solution; 
A,= Area of internal standard peak in the 
chromatogram of sample solution; and 
P= Percent purity of tricyclazole reference 
standard. 


A-2 HPLC METHOD 


A-2.1 Principle 


Tricyclazole content is determined by high performance 
liquid chromatography (HPLC) using internal standard 
technique. 


A-2.2 Apparatus 


A-2.2.1 High Performance Liquid Chromatograph, 
equipped with a constant flow (isocratic) pump, HPLC 
column heater compartment, sample injector capable 
of injecting 20 microlitre aliquots, ultraviolet detector 
and a chromatography software /printer-plotter cum 
integrator. 


A-2.2.2 Analytical Balance, (Least count 0.1 mg) 
A-2.2.3 Microlitre Syringe, 50 ul 


A-2.2.4 Filtration Apparatus, with 0.45 um membrane 
filters. 


A-2.2.5 Standard Glassware 


A-2.3 Chromatographic Conditions 


The suggested operative parameters are as follows, but 
can be changed if necessary, provided standardization 
is done. 


A-2.3.1 Column, C-18, 5u, particle size of 250 mm x 
4.6 mm, Stainless steel column or equivalent. 


A-2.3.2 Mobile Phase, Acetonitrile: Water (50 : 50, 
v/v), pH of water = 2.85, Adjusted with aqueous ortho 
phosphoric acid solution(10 percent). 


A-2.3.3 Flow Rate, 0.85 ml / min. 


A-2.3.4 Injection Volume, 20 y 1. 

A-2.3.5 UV Detector Wave Length, 231 nm. 

A-2.4. Reagents 

A-2.4.1 Acetonitrile, HPLC grade. 

A-2.4.2 Water, HPLC grade. 

A-2.4.3 Methanol, HPLC grade. 

A-2.4.4 Acetophenone (Internal Standard), AR grade. 


A-2.4.5 Tricyclazole Reference Standard, of known 
purity. 


A-2.4.6 Ortho Phosphoric Acid, HPLC grade 85 
percent. 


A-2.5 Preparation 


A-2.5.1 Preparation of Mobile Phase 


Adjust the pH of HPLC grade water to 2.85 with 
10 percent ortho phosphoric acid solution in water. Add 
filtered 1 000 ml of water (pH 2.85) to 1 000 ml of 
filtered acetonitrile in a flask, mix thoroughly. Sonicate 
for 15 min. 


A-2.5.2 Preparation of Internal Standard Solution 


Weigh about 1.5 g of acetophenone into a 100 ml 
volumetric flask. Make up to volume with HPLC grade 
acetonitrile and sonicate for 5 min. 


A-2.5.3 Standard Preparation 


Weigh accurately 50 mg of tricyclazole reference 
standard of known purity into a 100 ml volumetric flask. 
Add 50 ml methanol, sonicate for 5 min to dissolve the 
material. Pipette out 5 ml of internal standard solution 
into the volumetric flask. Make up the volume with 
Methanol and mix. Pipette out 1ml of diluted solution 
in a 100 ml volumetric flask and dilute up to the mark 
with mobile phase. 


A-2.5.4 Sample Preparation 


Weigh accurately sample equivalent to 50 mg of 
tricyclazole into a 100 ml volumetric flask. Add 50 ml 
methanol, sonicate for 5 min to dissolve tricyclazole. 
Pipette out 5 ml of internal standard solution into the 
volumetric flask. Make up the volume with methanol 
and mix. Filter through 0.45um membrane filter if 
required. Pipette out 1 ml of diluted solution in a 
100 ml volumetric flask and dilute up to the mark with 
mobile phase. 


A-2.6 Estimation 


Equilibrate the column with mobile phase for 45 min 
before commencement of analysis. After a stable 
baseline is obtained , inject the standard solution 
on to HPLC column, until area of tricyclazole and 


internal standard in replicate injections matches within 
+ 2 percent. Inject the standard and sample solution 
in accordance with A-2.6.1 and then compute the 
percentage purity of tricyclazole in WG sample using 
the formula given in A-2.8. 


A-2.6.1 Sequence of injection to be followed — C1, C2, 

SIA, S1B, C2, Cl, S2A, S2B, C2 

A-2.7 Retention Time (Indicative Values) 
Tricyclazole :~4.8 min 

Acetophenone : ~ 8.0 min (internal standard) 


Total run time : 10.0 min 


From the chromatograms of the standard solution and

M x4A,x4A,xP 
Tricyclazole content, % m/m = 


M,*A,* A,

solution; 


„= Mass in g, of sample taken for the test; 

Area of tricyclazole peak in the chromatograph 

of the standard solution; 

A,= Area of tricyclazole peak in the chromatograph 
of the sample solution;

ANNEX B 


[ Clause 3.3.1 and Table 1, SI No. (vi) ] 


DETERMINATION OF pH 


B-1 THEORY 


The pH of the aqueous sample is determined using a 
pH meter with combined glass electrode. 


B-2 APPARATUS 

B-2.1 Analytical Balance 

B-2.2 Measuring Cylinder, 100 ml, with stopper. 
B-2.3 Funnel (Glass) 

B-2.4 Beaker, 150 ml. 

B-2.5 Volumetric Flask. 

B-2.6 Test Tubes 

B-3 REAGENTS 


B-3.1 Standard Buffer Solutions, for calibration of 
pH meter. 


B-3.2 Distilled Water. 


B-4 PROCEDURE 


B-4.1 Weigh accurately of required quantity of the 
sample (1 g for 1 percent and 10 g for 10 percent) in 
a beaker and transfer it to a measuring cylinder with 
distilled water. 


B-4.2 Make up the volume to 100 ml with distilled 
water and shake vigorously until completely mixed or 
dispersed. 


B-4.3 If necessary, transfer the solution or dispersion 
to a beaker and allow any suspended material to settle 
for Imin. 


B-4.4 Immerse the electrode into the liquid and measure 
its pH without stirring. 


B-4.5 Record the pH value after Imin. if the pH value 
changes more than 0.1 pH unit during this equilibration 
time, record the pH 10 min after immersion of the 
electrode.
